rule YARA_CobaltStrike_Generic_Fixed {
    meta:
        description = "Detects Cobalt Strike beacons with reduced false positives"
        author = "SOC_Team"
        hash_whitelist = "a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2"

    strings:
        $beacon_config = { 2E 72 63 64 00 } // '.rcd' string in config
        $http_get = "GET / HTTP/1.1" wide
        $https_uri = "https://" wide
    condition:
        $beacon_config and $http_get and $https_uri and 
        not pe.imphash() in ("f34d5f2d4577ed6d9ceec516c1f5a744", "3d012e633526277c77f4236c31954221") and
        not md5(0, filesize) == "e5c3c0d7f8e4f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0"
}

arguments.summary: A spear-phishing campaign attributed to APT-41 (Double Dragon) resulted in the compromise of a high-criticality finance workstation (WS-FIN-042). The initial vector was a malicious email triggering an encoded PowerShell script via Outlook, leading to the execution of a ShadowPad variant through process hollowing and rundll32 abuse. The malware established C2 communication over HTTPS to a known-bad IP and attempted lateral movement via SMB. The threat was detected through IDS alerts and EDR telemetry, and containment actions included blocking the C2 IP at the firewall.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dynamic_DNS {
    meta:
        description = "Detects dynamically generated Cobalt Strike beacon domains via entropy and pattern"
        author = "SOC Team"
        date = "2026-04-09"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/004/"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $beacon_config = { 6A 00 68 [2] 00 00 68 [2] 00 00 6A 00 E8 } // Common beacon config stub
        $dns_query_high_entropy = /[a-z0-9]{12,}\.[a-z]{2,4}/
    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and // MZ header
        $beacon_config and
        #dns_query_high_entropy > 5
}
